items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Eli had saved for months to buy the bicycle in the shop window. When his friend's family lost their home in a fire, Eli quietly gave the money to help them instead. He kept riding his old, rusty bike without a word.

Claim A: Eli valued his friend's family more than the new bicycle. Claim B: Eli could not afford the new bicycle. Which claim is supported by evidence, and which is contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported, because Eli gave away the saved money to help his friend's family and kept his old bike. Claim B is contradicted, since the text says he had saved enough to buy the bicycle.

items.prompt:

Lucia always finished her chores before her siblings woke. When her mother praised her, Lucia just smiled and said the morning was the quietest time to think.

Claim A: Lucia enjoys quiet time in the morning. Claim B: Lucia dislikes her siblings. Which claim does the text support, and which goes beyond the evidence?
items.answer: Claim A is supported, because Lucia says the morning is 'the quietest time to think.' Claim B goes beyond the evidence; nothing in the text suggests she dislikes her siblings.

items.prompt:

The team captain, Rosa, passed the ball to the weakest player so he could finally score. The crowd did not notice, but the boy beamed for the rest of the game.

Claim A: Rosa wanted to help her teammate feel proud. Claim B: Rosa was a selfish player. Which claim is supported, and which is contradicted by the text?
items.answer: Claim A is supported, since Rosa gave up her own chance so the boy could score and feel proud. Claim B is contradicted, because her action shows generosity, not selfishness.

items.prompt:

Claim A: Dad wanted to repair the relationship. Claim B: Dad was still angry. Which claim does the evidence best support?
items.answer: Claim A is best supported; the breakfast and the note inviting a talk show Dad reaching out to repair things. Claim B is not supported, since the gestures point toward reconciliation rather than anger.
